text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's prosecutor general is expected to launch a criminal investigation into former prime minister Zhan Videnov on charges of sanctioning excessive wheat exports, which had led to a grain crisis in the country, Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said. @

-- Bulgaria is expected to seal today a preliminary funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) totalling $650 million and the first tranche of $77 million could be expected in April, a senior IMF envoy said.

-- Bulgaria hopes to sell a 60 percent stake in Chimko-Vratsa fertiliser producer for $100 million and a contract with a potential buyer is expected to be sealed at the beginning of April, Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev said. @
-- Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) said that over 300,000 Bulgarians voted on Saturday in UDF primary elections to nominate candidates to run in general elections on April 19.
-- Bulgaria's State Savings Bank (SSB), the country's largest savings institution, said it had asked the interim cabinet for a permission to attract foreign currency deposits.
Under current regulations the SSB can attract only lev deposits.

-- The U.S. Undersecretary of Defence for Policy Walter Slocombe arrived in Sofia to discuss Bulgaria's application to join NATO and bilateral military issues with President Petar Stoyanov and Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski.
-- Bulgaria's state carrier Balkan Airlines has contracted 1,320 charter flights to transport German tourists to Bulgaria in the summer, a Balkan senior official said.

-- Bulgaria's Social care ministry has proposed to the interim cabinet to grant 500,000 levs per person to people to be laid off under the government's restructuring programme of state loss-makers, Social care minister Ivan Neikov said.
The project is expected to be funded by a $30 million loan from the World Bank.
-- Bulgaria's private Unionbank raised capital by 990 million levs to 3.185 million levs, the bank's executive director Ivan Radev said.
